newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-OWN GOAL ENDS REAL MADRID'S DOUBLE DREAMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OWN GOAL ENDS REAL MADRID'S DOUBLE DREAMS.

text.p: Barcelona ended Real Madrid's dreams of a Spanish league and cup double with a 1-1 draw in a dramatic Spanish Cup fourth round tie on Thursday.
The result in their opponents' Bernabeu Stadium gave Barcelona a 4-3 win on aggregate.
The decisive moment came after 69 minutes when Barcelona's Brazilian striker Ronaldo broke clear down the left wing, leaving behind his marker and compatriot Roberto Carlos.
Ronaldo's first shot hit the post but it rebounded to his feet and his second effort was turned into his own net by the luckless Carlos.
Real Madrid equalised nine minutes later when Croatian striker David Suker was scythed down in the penalty area by Blanc and Suker blasted home the spot kick.
Barcelona defended solidly in the final minutes despite fierce Real pressure to keep the scores level and ensure they went into the next round.
Real though had only themselves to blame for their demise after a scoreless first half in which they had the Barcelona goal under almost permanent siege but failed to score.
Italian International Christian Panucci was a constant threat down the right wing and Clarence Seedorf provided ample service through the middle to the Real forwards.
Both Raul and Suker squandered a number of clear chances in front of goal or were denied by a series of theatrical saves from Barcelona's Portuguese international goalkeeper Vitor Baia.
Real's best chance of the first half was after 33 minutes when the Barcelona defender Ferrer failed to pick up Roberto Carlos.
The Brazilian provided a superb cross from the left wing but Suker mistimed his header with only Baia to beat.
Earlier, Rayo Vallecano won 2-1 away at Extremadura to ensure that at least two Madrid sides went through to the quarter finals. Rayo joined Atletico who beat Compostela on Tuesday.
